title: Assurance Nudge Logbook - control schematic side notes (Davion)
body:
Purpose:
quick, messy working notes for control mapping and lightweight evidence ideas. not a final narrative — mostly thinking out loud so i can hand off to maya for vetting next week.

Top-level goals (what i want out of this doc):
- sketch which infra hooks can generate reliable artifacts for SOC2 evidence (not just screenshots).
- flag low-cost automation experiments to reduce manual evidence collection.
- list outstanding questions to resolve with infra and sre.

Control buckets i'm eyeballing (very rough):
- access management (user provisioning, least privilege, joiners/leavers)
  - existing signals: provisioning logs from okta (SCIM), terraform state changes, GCP IAM audit logs.
  - evidence candidates: okta SCIM audit CSV for period, terraform plan/apply history with PR links, daily IAM-change report (scriptable).
  - quick win: scheduled export of okta audit -> signed blob in GCS, rotate monthly.

- change management (PR review, approvals, deploys)
  - signals: GitHub protected branches, CODEOWNERS, merge metadata, Circle/Buildkite deployments, release tags.
  - evidence candidates: merge commit list + review diffs, deployment run ids, canary rollout notes.
  - open q: what retention do we need for CI logs? storage cost tradeoff (ask finance).

- monitoring & incident response
  - signals: pagerduty incident logs, alerting rules in prometheus, oncall schedule snapshots.
  - evidence: incident postmortems (redacted if needed), alert definition export, oncall rotation export.
  - experiment: attach a stable incident-id label to related artifacts (e.g., PRs, slack thread) to simplify bundling.

- encryption & key management
  - signals: KMS audit for key usage, HSM attestations where used, env var references.
  - evidence: KMS access logs for period, policy docs, KMS rotation schedule.
  - note: for private deployments customers may manage keys; doc needs branching.

- backups & recovery
  - signals: snapshot timestamps, backup-job logs, restore-test run results.
  - evidence: latest snapshot manifest for period + notes on restore test.
  - todo: set quarterly restore test owner and add to calendar invites.

Automation ideas (low effort / high signal):
1) 'evidence-bundle' job: cron job that runs monthly and packages named artifacts (okta export, KMS logs snippet, PR list) into a dated zip with checksum + storage path. Attach to a small confluence stub with checklist.
2) badge for PRs: add a CI job that enforces a "security-checklist" label; checklist checklist items map to control IDs. Provides a quick grepable artifact.
3) incident-tag aggregator: small lambda that watches PD incidents and collects attachments (PR links, slack permalink, deploy id) into a single JSON. reduces manual collection.

Open questions / blockers:
- retention policy: what retention windows legal/compliance expects vs what infra can reasonably store? (ask legal + finance)
- who will own the monthly evidence-bundle? are we comfortable making it a trust-ops job or handoff to platform-engineering?
- scope creep risk: do we keep customer-specific private deployment evidence separate or create a template?
- PII/redaction: automatic redaction routine needed for incident PMs before attaching to evidence bundles. who signs off?

Immediate next steps (short horizon):
- Monday: sync 30m with Maya to align on owners for each bucket. (davion -> schedule)
- Tue: prototype okta export cron + GCS drop for one month window. tag: PROTO-OKTA.
- Wed: draft confluence stub that describes evidence-bundle format and example zip contents. link to JIRA: TRUST-1423.
- End of week: demo prototype to lena and platform-eng lead, collect feedback.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- prefer machine-verifiable artifacts (logs, exports, checksums) over screenshots.
- when in doubt, include a tiny narrative file in the bundle that explains context (who ran it, what timeframe, redactions applied).
- minimize special-case ad-hoc evidence. invest in small pipelines that are reusable across controls.

Potential owners i think fit (rough):
- okta/identity exports: platform-engineering (owner: Priya)
- PR/CI artefacts: developer-experience (owner: Ahmed)
- deployment/infra logs: infra team (owner: Rowan)
- incident aggregation: trust-ops (owner: Maya)

Reference links / quick pointers:
- confluence draft: TRUST-Design-Controls-2026 (will update after prototype)
- slack: #trust-ops, #infra-deploys for follow-ups
- jira: TRUST-1423 (evidence-bundle prototype)

Random friction points i expect:
- teams are protective of long-term log retention because of cost -> need to present unit-cost estimate per S3/GCS-month.
- some evidence requires correlating artifacts across systems (e.g., PR -> deploy id -> runtime logs). we need a stable crosswalk key (i propose using commit hash + deploy id).

Last thought: build one small repeatable pipeline (okta -> monthly bundle) and iterate. wins build momentum and gives concrete PRs for SOC2 reviewers.

End of notes.
summary: working scratchbook for low-friction evidence collection ideas and control mapping; prototype okta export -> bundle is next.
